task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
Thanks for the details — that's helpful. Right now the phone shows three things that would keep data from working properly:

1. **Mobile data is turned OFF** — data can't work at all
2. **Network is on 2G** — far too slow for data
3. **A VPN is connected** — this can throttle speeds significantly

Let's fix these one at a time, starting with mobile data.

**Step 1: Turn mobile data ON**
- On your phone, go to Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network
- Switch **Mobile data** to **ON**
- (Or just pull down the quick settings shade and tap the "Mobile data" tile)

Once that's done, let me know and I'll walk you through the next step (switching off 2G).

Good — mobile data is on now. Next let's deal with Data Saver, which restricts background data and can make things feel slow even with an active connection.

**Step 2: Turn Data Saver OFF**
- Go to Settings → Network & Internet → **Data Saver**
- Switch it to **OFF** (if prompted, confirm)

Let me know once that's off, and then we'll move on to getting you off 2G onto a faster network — that's the biggest factor here.

**Step 3: Switch off 2G onto a faster network**

2G is far too slow for mobile data — this is almost certainly why things are crawling. Let's set your phone to prefer 4G/5G:

- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Preferred network mode** (sometimes called "Network mode" or "Preferred network type")
- Select **4G/5G preferred** (may be listed as "LTE/5G" or "5G auto")

If you can't find that menu, tell me your phone's make and model and I'll give you the exact path.

Once you've switched it, your phone should reconnect on a faster network. Let me know what the status bar shows then — and we'll tackle the VPN after that.

Great progress — 5G with excellent signal and data enabled is the best-case setup. Regarding the VPN: it can be left on if it isn't hurting your speeds, but it's the one remaining thing that could throttle your connection.

**Step 4: Check your actual speed**
- Run a **speed test** on your phone (open a browser and search "speed test", or use your carrier's speed test tool)

Let me know the result:
- If it comes back **Excellent** — you're all set, and you can keep the VPN on.
- If it comes back **Poor**, **Fair**, or **Good** — the VPN is likely the culprit, and we'll disconnect it in the next step.

Everything on the network side looks correct, and the only remaining item that can block data outright is the VPN. A connected VPN that isn't actually passing traffic will produce exactly this — full signal, 5G, data enabled, but "No Connection" on a speed test.

**Step 5: Disconnect the VPN**
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN**
- Tap the connected VPN (it may show a gear/settings icon next to it)
- Tap **Disconnect**

If you use a third-party VPN app (NordVPN, ExpressVPN, etc.), you can instead open that app and tap **Disconnect** there.

Once it's disconnected, please run the speed test again and tell me the result. If it comes back with a speed this time, we're done. If it still says "No Connection," let me know and we'll dig further.
I understand the frustration — you've done everything right so far. Let me re-verify things on the account side before we try the next fix, just to be certain nothing there is blocking you.

I checked your line and device on my end — everything looks healthy:

- **Line L1002 (555-123-2002):** Active, not suspended, contract valid through 2026-12-31, your 2 GB refuel is applied
- **Device:** Smartphone Pro Max, activated, IMEI on file
- **Roaming:** already enabled on the line

So the account and line side are fine. The one remaining device setting that can cause "full signal but no data" is your **APN settings** — these are the settings your phone uses to actually reach the carrier's data network, and if they're wrong you'll see exactly what you're seeing: strong 5G signal but no data traffic.

**Step 6: Check your APN settings**
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Advanced → Access Point Names (APN)**
- Look at the APN currently selected and its **MMSC** field
- Tell me what the APN name shows, and whether the MMSC field is filled in or blank

If the APN comes back as incorrect or the MMSC is missing, I'll have you reset the APN to defaults and then reboot the phone — that combination clears this problem in most cases.
Let me check one more thing on your account before we go further.

Yes, those APN settings look properly configured — the APN name is set and the MMSC URL is populated, so that's not the problem.

I also verified on my end that your line is **Active**, not suspended, your contract runs through 2026-12-31, and there are no overdue bills that would restrict service. So everything on the account side is clear.

You've now worked through every setting I'd check: airplane mode off, SIM active, mobile data on, Data Saver off, 5G preferred, VPN disconnected, APN configured, and your data refuel applied.

**Step 7: Reboot your device**

You did reboot earlier, but that was before we changed the network mode to 5G and disconnected the VPN — those changes need a fresh restart to fully settle in.

- Press and hold the power button, then tap **Restart**
- Wait for the phone to fully boot back up
- Check that the status bar shows excellent signal and 5G
- Run the speed test again

Please let me know what the speed test reports after the reboot. If it still comes back "No Connection" after this, I'll escalate you to our technical support team so they can run deeper diagnostics on the line — but let's try the reboot first.
